Lessons.Title: Attributes of Triangles and Quadrilaterals
ExplanationParagraphs: 2021 Grade3 Unit7 Lesson2 original owner-device lesson.html SHA256 a617a149382a5abd275324c47e71a53b8af3e92e3ca15976146a462b888b815d and preparation.html SHA256 1f9288c292f16ae9ad88d0344ab597b4aa8517681cd05579026bd051607c15c5 examined. Three original student-facing sections were mapped. The separate publisher Triangle Cards Grade3 and Quadrilateral Cards Grade3 blackline masters, publisher image pixels and independent Student Task Statements PDF are NOT pixel or page compared. Therefore source-to-first-party work is semantic and teacher-gated, not a claim of complete card parity.

Warm-up True or False: Multiples of Ten (10 minutes) has exactly FOUR original assertions: 3×60=9×10 FALSE because180≠90; 180=3×60 TRUE;6×40=24×10 TRUE because240=240;24×10=240 TRUE. Encourage place-value distributive and associative reasoning rather than only computing both sides; all four exact numeric truth values can be machine checked.

Activity1 Card Sort: Triangles (15 minutes), one teacher-prepared TRIANGLE CARD set per group of TWO OR FOUR, copied on distinctive colored paper to avoid confusion with quad cards. Since ALL cards are triangles, sorting by 'three sides' does not separate them meaningfully. Student chooses finer attributes: number of equal-length sides (all three, two, none), presence of one right angle, or visual size and shape equivalence. The source doesn't require formal words equilateral/isosceles/scalene to be introduced, but teacher may allow a pupil who already knows them. Teacher can supply a ruler when equal-length distinctions aren't visually evident. No one immutable subset assignment without inspecting card pictures.

Activity2 Card Sort: Quadrilaterals (20 minutes) supplies the original SECOND independent set with TWENTY shapes, ALL quadrilaterals, groups of2 or4. Pupils sort into categories by equal side lengths, number of right angles and, in their own words, sides that run in the same direction. They are NOT expected to use the formal term parallel yet. The original physical quadrilateral cards are stored in bags/envelopes to reuse in next lesson and centers; first-party content should not randomly re-number cards or substitute a generic unrelated worksheet.

Activity2 additionally requires a GALLERY CHECK: groups DISPLAY sorted card arrangements and visit another group's display to infer its categorization rule before groups explain. Retain this cross-group observation rather than just listing shape type definitions. Source synthesis compares which properties work for triangles AND quadrilaterals and which differ: triangles have at most ONE right angle, while quadrilaterals may have multiple; triangles cannot have a pair of sides going in same direction when closed, unlike some quads. Teacher checks pupils can state their chosen grouping rationale and test it on original displayed cards.

Source public teacher guidance MLR2 collects words for equal side lengths and right angles, and supports spatial explanations with rulers/gestures. The teacher-gated Cool-down Describe the Shape and original blackline card sets are NOT accessed in this first-party implementation; .NET tests, Stage D, academic review and runtime verification have not been completed.

The original physical triangle and quadrilateral card masters, source-image pixels and standalone pupil PDFs were not inspected. Teacher supervision of the actual cards is required and first-party substitutes are not source-identical.

KeyConcepts.Title: Triangles have three sides
KeyConcepts.Definition: All cards in source triangle activity are triangles.
KeyConcepts.Rule: To make meaningful subgroups, use length or corner properties beyond side count.
KeyConcepts.Example: Triangles with all equal side lengths versus triangles with no equal sides.

KeyConcepts.Title: Quadrilaterals have four sides
KeyConcepts.Definition: Original source has20 quadrilateral cards, each with four sides.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Compare equal side lengths, right angles and side direction.
KeyConcepts.Example: Some quadrilaterals have several right angles.

KeyConcepts.Title: Right-angle classification
KeyConcepts.Rule: A triangle can have at most one right angle; quadrilaterals may have more.
KeyConcepts.Example: Teacher compares whether right angles occur.

KeyConcepts.Title: Open shape classification
KeyConcepts.Definition: Multiple groupings can be correct if property-based and consistently applied.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Teacher examines actual card diagrams and category reasons.
KeyConcepts.Example: One quad may belong to both equal-sided and right-angle groups.

WorkedExamples.Title: Triangle subgroups
WorkedExamples.Question: How should identical three-sided polygons be distinguished further?
WorkedExamples.Method: Look at side length equality and right-angle presence.
Steps: Look for any square-type right corner.
Explain each chosen grouping in class.
WorkedExamples.Check: Use original cards, not an invented exact per-card mapping.

WorkedExamples.Title: Quadrilateral gallery
WorkedExamples.Question: Can classmates recognize another group's quad sort?
WorkedExamples.Method: Look for equal sides/right angles/same-direction edges.
Steps: Inspect displayed20 source quad cards as sorted.
State a plausible property explaining members.
Ask group to verify its own classification.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Multiple valid category choices with evidence
WorkedExamples.Check: Teacher verifies original card art and reason.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Call the first warm-up multiplication statement true.
Require every triangle be in one category because all have three sides.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The goal is SUB-categories using further properties.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Compare side lengths or right angles.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Teach formal 'parallel' terminology as mandatory here.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The source says students aren't expected to know that term.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assign a fixed published grouping without checking actual card faces.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Two original blackline card sets not inspected.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Teacher checks pupil grouping against real source physical shapes.

SummaryPoints: Source Activity1 colored paper Triangle Cards Grade3, groups of2 or4, classify by same side lengths/right angle; no mandatory higher terms.
Source Activity2 TWENTY Quadrilateral Cards Grade3, groups of2 or4, classify by lengths/right angles/same-direction sides, then gallery infer another group's rule.
Original source card masters, student PDF, Cool-down and images not certified; tests authored only.
